clue.text: Like the pure in heart, more up and about?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: the clue works by contraries: being up is the opposite of being in bed, so up cues the bed you are out of
by the same contrary logic, more cues its opposite, less

explanation.surface: A question whether the saintly are livelier and more active than the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius works by contraries: being more up and about is the same as lying less in bed, so 'about' puts one around the other. The definition alludes to the Beatitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes say the pure in heart are blessed, so the word describes them exactly.

clue.text: Bishop starts to preside over church with a meal …

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run something is to take charge of it, presiding over it

explanation.surface: A bishop taking charge of a church that comes with a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into the next two clues, which describe the same meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: … which is the same as …

parts.note: a plain description of a verb meaning matches or is equivalent to

explanation.walkthrough: A link in the chain from 1 to 3 down: the meal equals a square meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To equal something is to be identical in value or amount to it.

clue.text: … are many involved in cooking of 2

indicators.note: the pieces are tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
the answer to 2 down

explanation.surface: Ending a chain about a meal: many things go into cooking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' mixes ARE, M and the 2-down answer into one ten-letter anagram; the chain reads: brunch ... equals ... a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is a full, substantial one, which a cooked brunch is.

clue.text: Headquarters of French vessel

parts.note: de is French for of
a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.surface: The head office of a French shipping company.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base or storage centre, a headquarters for supplies or troops.

clue.text: Henry the first has only fish

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
the first is written as the Roman numeral I, as in Henry I
only in the sense of merely means but, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A claim that King Henry I owned nothing but a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas, a specific example of a fish.

clue.text: Greek citizens' interjections to take notice over voting?

indicators.note: the two calls stand over and around the voting, enclosing it

parts.note: hoi is a shout to attract attention
oi is another shout to make someone take notice
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Ancient Greeks calling out to each other to attend to an election.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Greek for 'the many', the ordinary citizens; the possessive in the clue is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Greek for 'the many', meaning the common people or the masses.

clue.text: Don't work for your bread!

definitions.meaning: to idle or lounge about rather than labour
a single baked block of bread

explanation.definitionFit: To idle about is to do no work, and a baked block of bread is the noun sense.

clue.text: Sweepers catching journalist in compromising places?

indicators.note: the sweepers catch the journalist, holding it inside

parts.note: brooms are sweeping brushes
ED is the abbreviation for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman caught in a scandal by tabloid snoops.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught in someone's bedroom is the classic compromising situation.

clue.text: It's wrong to go on French river as a slow mover

indicators.note: one piece is placed on, after, the other in the down answer

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river of northern France

explanation.surface: A slow creature saying it's wrong to travel along a river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise is proverbially slow, as in the fable of the hare and the tortoise.

clue.text: Ben bends over for freedom

indicators.note: the bends are draped over the name, so they sit on either side of it

parts.note: two U-bends give two letters U
Ben-Hur is the title hero of the novel and film, so Ben gives Hur

explanation.surface: A man called Ben bending down to win his liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is not a name to keep but half of Ben-Hur, leaving HUR; the plural 'bends' gives a U on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swahili word for freedom, used as a slogan of Kenyan independence.

clue.text: Royal couple make love?

parts.note: Prince Philip, Phil for short, is half of the royal couple
the joining word between the two names of the couple
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the other half of the couple

explanation.surface: An invitation for the Queen and Prince Philip to be romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is spelt out as 'Phil and ER': Phil for Prince Philip, ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, so the question mark softens make love.

clue.text: Speech by officer about arrangement of shades

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, a military officer
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A colonel giving a lecture on how to arrange colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloration is the pattern or scheme of colours, here in the American spelling.

clue.text: State where one may advance in board 21?

definitions.text: where one may advance in board 21?
definitions.meaning: 21 is game, so a board game; in Monopoly a card tells you to advance ...

explanation.surface: Asking where a nation might move forward in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 21 makes 'board game'; the Monopoly card 'Advance to Go' supplies the phrase TO GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a republic in West Africa, a sovereign country.

clue.text: Stone makes loser itchy

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A gemstone that brings someone who loses out in a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrysolite is an old name for olivine or peridot, a green gemstone.

clue.text: Roadhouses?

parts.note: read literally, houses that travel on the road, ie caravans

explanation.definitionFit: Caravans and trailer homes are dwellings built to be towed along roads.

clue.text: Screen lifer, ill at heart, with time becomes striking

indicators.note: the illness lies at the heart of the name, inside it

parts.note: Monty Python's Life of Brian put Brian's life on screen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star, sick inside, who in time becomes dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen lifer' is the hero of the Monty Python film Life of Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means dazzlingly bright or outstanding, so very striking.

clue.text: Desiring excitement, come here for a fight

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Fight fans come to the front, wanting thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringside is the area next to a boxing ring, where spectators gather to watch.

clue.text: One county set off with 99, identical but different

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: set off means the word set is removed from the county

parts.note: Somerset is a county in south-west England
IC is read as 99 in Roman numerals, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A county side setting out with 99 runs, the same yet not the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'county set off' is Somerset minus SET, leaving SOMER; IC as 99 is a loose Roman form.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomers share the same atoms but differ in arrangement, so they are alike yet unlike.

clue.text: This month shows skill with lack of firmness

parts.note: inst, short for instant, means this month in old business letters
ability is skill or competence

explanation.surface: A monthly report that a skilled performer is wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) was the commercial abbreviation for 'of this month' in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsteady or unstable means lacking firmness.

clue.text: Sad comment on car's state

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark on the condition of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state.

clue.text: The devil's about right for a companion

indicators.note: the devil goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: a fiend is a devil

explanation.surface: The devil is around looking for someone to keep company with.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend is a close companion.

clue.text: Recreation one gets from crossing America?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asking what fun you might have travelling across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'crossing' and the start of 'America'.
explanation.definitionFit: A game is a pastime played for amusement, a form of recreation.

clue.text: Manual arrest by copper?

parts.note: police are 'the boys in blue', so blue stands for a copper
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A policeman making an arrest by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar work is manual labour, as opposed to office work.

clue.text: What editor does for setter in the finish?

indicators.note: the setter is placed in the finish

parts.note: an end is a finish
the crossword setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An editor's job is to check the setter's work at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text, which is an editor's task.

clue.text: Dame could be Dane with English genes

parts.note: DNA is the material genes are made of

explanation.surface: A titled lady could be a Dane with English ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be Dane' also signals an anagram of DANE, a second route to the same letters; Dame Edna Everage was Barry Humphries's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edna Everage was the comic character played by Barry Humphries.

clue.text: What waves do with anger about wireless curtailment

indicators.note: the angry word goes round the shortened wireless

parts.note: anger suggests being irate, the adjective for angry

indicators.note: curtailing cuts off the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: wireless is the old word for radio

explanation.surface: How radio waves behave when furious at having a transmission cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailment' cuts the final O from the old word for radio, and 'about' wraps the angry word around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiation is waves of energy that shine on or bombard a target, which is to irradiate it.

clue.text: Is to prosecute a matter for decision?

parts.note: taken as written
to sue is to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: Asking whether a court case is something still to be decided.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a question or point in dispute that awaits a ruling.

clue.text: Spell letter by church worker

parts.note: en is the name of the letter N (a printer's measure)
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A letter written by someone working at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to put under a spell; spell here is a verb meaning bewitch.

clue.text: One had red tendency? Far from it!

definitions.text: One had red tendency? Far from it!

indicators.note: the letters end up far from where they started, rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting they were never a communist sympathiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-&lit: a diehard conservative is far from having a red tendency, and 'One had red' rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard resists change stubbornly, the opposite of a radical or left-leaning person.
